title: Dead Stop
body:
You are out of fuel. The ship drifts. The stars do not care.

The ship computer calculates your trajectory. You are going somewhere. It will take four hundred years. The destination is not where you wanted to go.

The emergency beacon, if you have one, becomes the only option. The rescue may be friendly. It may not. It will definitely be expensive.
epitaph: They ran out of fuel. The emergency beacon was in cargo the whole time.

title: Structural Failure
body:
The hull failed. The ship computer's final log entry is two words: 'Hull compromised.'

The entry does not capture the sound. It does not capture the three seconds between the sound and the silence. It captures the timestamp, which is precise. The precision feels like the wrong thing to preserve.
epitaph: The ship held together until it didn't. The crop was still growing when the hull gave way.

title: Autopilot
body:
There is nobody left to fly the ship.

The ship computer engages autopilot. The crop continues to grow. The navigation continues to function. The ship arrives at its destination on schedule, precisely, with a living crop and no living crew.

The colony authority's report notes this as a 'partial success.' The definition of 'partial' is doing remarkable work.
epitaph: The ship arrived. The crop arrived. Nobody else did. The colony authority filed it under 'logistics.'

title: Management Restructuring
body:
Morale has collapsed. The crew has voted. You have been relieved of command.

The vote was unanimous, which is impressive given that the crew could not agree on anything else for the entire journey. The ship computer logs this as 'leadership transition' which is technically accurate.

You are confined to quarters. The crew flies the ship. They are, it turns out, fine at this. The ship arrives. You are asked to fill out an exit survey.
epitaph: The crew mutinied. The captain filed a complaint. The complaint is still pending.

title: Empty Growbay
body:
The crop is dead.

The growbay lights continue to cycle. The water system continues to run. The nutrient feed continues to drip. Everything works. Nothing grows.

The ship computer updates the mission status. The word it uses is 'compromised.' The crew knows what this means. The mission was the crop. The crop is gone. You can still fly. You can still arrive. You will arrive with nothing to plant.

The ship continues toward the destination. The growbay stays lit. Nobody turns it off. Turning it off would mean something nobody is ready to say.
epitaph: They arrived. They brought nothing that grows. The growbay lights were still on.

continue_option.narrative: You keep flying. There is nothing else to do. The destination is ahead. What you bring to it has changed. What it means to arrive has changed. But the ship still flies. And you are still in it.

title: Form Letter
body:
You missed the deadline. The colony slot has been reassigned.

A form letter arrives via long-range communication. It thanks you for your interest in the colonization program. It regrets to inform you that your allocated settlement zone has been assigned to another mission. It wishes you well in future endeavors.

The form letter is clearly automated. It was sent before you could have read it. The colony authority planned for this outcome. They planned for it because it happens often. You are not special. This is, somehow, the worst part.
epitaph: They arrived late. The planet had moved on. The form letter was already written.
